title: Part Thirty: Fraternities, Witches and the Forbidden Arts

sections.brief: Rosicrucian manifestos (Fama c.1610/1614, Confessio 1615 with its anti-papal language, Chymical Wedding 1616; Andreae's 'ludibrium'; Haslmayr's galley sentence; Paris 1623 and Naudé; no papal act found); Freemasonry from 1717; In eminenti 28 April 1738, Providas 18 March 1751, Humanum genus 20 April 1884, 1917 can. 2335, 1983 can. 1374, CDF 26 Nov 1983, DDF note 13 Nov 2023 (status as of Oct 2026); P2 (link vt10). Figures: fig-time, fig-compare

Bavarian Illuminati 1 May 1776 (Weishaupt, aims, grades, Knigge, membership estimates 650-2,500), Bavarian electoral edicts 1784, 1785, 1787, papers published 1787; myth's growth (Barruel and Robison 1797-98; Simonini letter 1806 as the antisemitic graft, Le Contemporain 1878, Protocols, Taxil 1885-97, Tusquets, Robertson 1991) named and refuted. Figures: fig-compare, fig-flow

Summis desiderantes 5 Dec 1484; Malleus (Kramer, 1486/87; Cologne approbation disputed; condemned 1490; Inquisition denied it authority); 40,000-60,000 executions (named estimates), ~80% women, half in the Empire; secular and prince-bishops' courts (Würzburg ~900); Roman Inquisition restraint, Salazar and the 1614 Spanish rules; nine-million myth (Voigt 1784) and midwife-witch myth (Harley 1990); cunning folk. Figures: fig-stats, fig-compare

Alchemy (Spondent quas non exhibent c.1317 = fraud law; Newton's million words); astrology and divination (Trent Rule IX 1564, Coeli et terrae 1586, Urban VIII 1631 and Morandi); tarot (game c.1440, sermon c.1450-70, divination from 1781, Etteilla, Golden Dawn, Rider-Waite-Smith 1909); the Index 1559-1966; Catechism 2116-2117 today; Sophia's 'why forbidden' claim tested, with one labelled interpretation. Figures: fig-compare, fig-time
